Subject: RFI: Dedicated reservation slotting & pricing lifecycle — EdgeScale

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this RFI. We're putting together our procurement package and need granular answers around how Redwood would slot our committed capacity over time given a mixed GPU demand profile. High-level asks:

- How do you recommend we apportion reservation slots across A100/RTX/quantized families to hit a 95% throughput target for our mix?
- What is the lifecycle for pricing changes during a multi-year reservation (annual repricing, add-on bursts, GPU family substitution)?
- If we need to change our committed mix mid-contract, what are the typical lead times and cost impacts?

I've attached our latest forecast workbook (ES_Capacity_Workbook_v3.xlsx) — page 2 has 6-month peak/99th quantile shapes. Can you also confirm if Redwood supports per-deal slotting rules (e.g., reserve X% for tail-burst lanes, Y% for stable routing)?

We'd like a short written response we can include in our RFP packet. Could you loop in technical and pricing leads?

Thanks,
Sarah Liao
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeScale AI

Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated reservation slotting & pricing lifecycle — EdgeScale

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the workbook — helpful detail. High-level answer up front: yes, Redwood supports per-deal slotting rules and a multi-tier lifecycle for pricing and GPU-family substitution. Below is a concise write-up you can quote in the RFP; I also attached our slotting playbook and a worked example mapped to your sheet.

Summary (for RFP):
- Slotting approach: We recommend a two-layer slotting model — 1) Stable pool (70–80%): provisioned on high-throughput A100-class slots for latency-sensitive production inference; 2) Flex/burst pool (20–30%): composed of mixed RTX/quantized families for cost-efficient tail and batch workloads. This split hits the 95% throughput target in your forecast shapes with typical 15–20% headroom for burst.
- Lifecycle & pricing: Commitment pricing is fixed per quarter for the committed baseline. Annual reviews allow repricing for add-ons or if a customer elects an upgrade to a new GPU family; GPU substitutions for availability reasons are offered with a priced uplift/rate card mapping and a 30–90 day notice depending on scale.
- Mid-contract changes: Rebalancing committed mix is supported; lead time depends on pool utilization. For changes <=20% of committed capacity, typical lead time is 30 days and no breakage fee; for >20% or cross-family conversions, we apply prorated adjustments and a 90-day capacity scheduling window.

Attached: Redwood_Slotting_Playbook_v1.2.xlsx — contains sample slot allocation calculations tied to your 6-month peak profiles. See tab 'EdgeScale example' for a mapping to ES_Capacity_Workbook_v3.xlsx.

Next steps: Karthik can follow up with throughput mapping and a GPU-fitment matrix; Dev will propose an illustrative pricing cadence and DocuSign-ready quote.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Dev —
Internal notes to prepare the procurement reply:

- Billing cadence: we do monthly invoicing with price protections applied quarterly (i.e., the invoice reflects the current quarter's locked pricing). That matches most enterprise buyers. Reply point: "monthly invoices; quarterly pricing lock for the committed baseline."
- Substitutions: propose a 0–15% uplift band for upward substitutions (e.g., A100 -> RTX+quantized isn't a direct uplift; map via token-equivalent throughput). We need to include a table tying each GPU family to a throughput coefficient (we'll pull from the kernel fit workbook). Karthik to produce the throughput coefficients (A100x1.0, H100x1.25, RTX-x0.65, INT8-x0.35)
- Tail-burst billing: recommend carving tail-burst as a consumption lane billed at a discounted per-token rate relative to on-demand (30% below on-demand) and capped monthly to avoid runaway charges.
- MSAs & redlines: we can commit to a 7 business day turnaround for first pass on standard enterprise MSA.

I'll draft a short procurement-friendly reply and attach the pricing estimate.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: RFI: Slotting scenario, pricing lifecycle & reservation RFI — Redwood response

Hi Ben / Sarah —

Thanks — please find a concise procurement-ready response below and an attached pricing estimate and SLA document for inclusion in your packet.

1) Billing cadence: Monthly invoices; pricing for the committed baseline is locked per quarter and reflected on each monthly invoice. Add-ons and consumption lanes are billed monthly in arrears.

2) GPU substitutions & uplift: We provide a pre-defined uplift matrix in the contract. Example mapping (illustrative):
- A100 -> H100: +12% uplift
- A100 -> RTX (quantized lane): -40% relative to A100 (throughput-equivalent mapping applied)
Mappings are applied via throughput coefficients to preserve economic parity; we include the full table in the attached PDF.

3) Tail-burst lanes: Carved out as a consumption lane by default. Billed monthly at a discounted rate (30% below on-demand) with a soft cap tied to committed baseline (configurable per-deal).

4) Mid-contract changes: Rebalancing <=20%: 30-day scheduling window, no breakage fee. >20% or cross-family conversions: 90-day scheduling window with prorated adjustments.

5) MSA redlines: Redwood commits to a 7 business-day first pass on standard enterprise MSA redlines, with exceptions escalated to legal.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_pricing_estimate.pdf, Redwood_Dedicated_SLOs.pdf

We can also produce a short section you can paste into the RFP under 'Slotting & Pricing lifecycle' if you'd like. If this aligns, Dev will generate a DocuSign-ready quote and I can schedule a quick wrap-up call next week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Account Executive
